questions.question:
The Deployment of the `orders-db` database in the namespace `orders` was deleted together with its PVC. Its data still lives on the PersistentVolume `orders-pv`, whose reclaim policy is `Retain`, so it is now in the `Released` state.

1. Make `orders-pv` available again **without deleting or recreating it**
2. Create a PVC named `orders-data` in `orders` (`ReadWriteOnce`, `500Mi`, StorageClass `manual`) that binds to `orders-pv`
3. The original manifest is saved at `/tmp/exam/q1/orders-db.yaml` on `cka-q1`. Edit that file so the container mounts `orders-data` at `/var/lib/mysql` (volume name `data`), then apply it

The Deployment `orders-db` must be available.

verification.description: orders-pv was reused (not recreated) and is Bound to orders-data
orders-db.yaml mounts orders-data and the Deployment is available

questions.question:
Argo CD must be deployed by a GitOps pipeline from a pre-rendered manifest. Its CRDs are managed separately, so they must **not** be part of the manifest.

1. Add the Helm repository `https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm` under the name `argo`
2. Create the namespace `argocd`
3. Render the chart `argo/argo-cd` version `7.7.3` for the namespace `argocd` with the release name `argocd`, configuring the chart so that it does not include its CRDs
4. Save the rendered manifest to `/tmp/exam/q2/argocd.yaml` on `cka-q2`

Do **not** install the chart into the cluster.

Hint: `--skip-crds` is not enough for every chart; check the chart's values.

verification.description: Repository argo points to the Argo Helm repo
argocd.yaml renders argo-cd 7.7.3 for argocd without CRDs
Namespace argocd exists and the chart is not installed

questions.question:
The Deployment `invoice-api` in the namespace `billing` writes its log to `/var/log/invoice/app.log`, which nobody can read with `kubectl logs`.

Update the Deployment (do not recreate it under another name):

1. Add an `emptyDir` volume named `logs` and mount it at `/var/log/invoice` in the existing `api` container
2. Add a **native sidecar** named `log-shipper` (image `busybox:1.36`, an init container with `restartPolicy: Always`) that mounts `logs` at the same path and runs `tail -F /var/log/invoice/app.log`

`kubectl logs deploy/invoice-api -n billing -c log-shipper` must show the application's log lines.

verification.description: Deployment has the logs volume and the log-shipper native sidecar
Sidecar streams the application log

questions.question:
The Deployment `checkout` in the namespace `checkout` already defines CPU requests.

Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named `checkout-hpa` (API `autoscaling/v2`) that:

- targets the Deployment `checkout`
- keeps between `2` and `8` replicas
- scales on an average CPU utilization of `60%`
- uses a scale-down stabilization window of `120` seconds

Hint: `kubectl autoscale` cannot set the behavior; generate a manifest and edit it.

verification.description: HPA targets checkout with 2-8 replicas at 60% CPU
Scale-down stabilization window is 120s

questions.question:
cert-manager's CRDs have been installed in the cluster.

1. Write the names of **all** cert-manager CRDs (one per line, just the names) to `/tmp/exam/q5/crds.txt` on `cka-q5`
2. Using `kubectl explain`, save the documentation of the field `spec.subject` of the `Certificate` resource to `/tmp/exam/q5/subject.txt`

verification.description: crds.txt lists exactly the cert-manager CRDs
subject.txt documents Certificate spec.subject

questions.question:
Several user-defined PriorityClasses exist in the cluster (ignore the built-in `system-*` classes).

1. Create a PriorityClass named `urgent` whose value is exactly **one less** than the highest user-defined PriorityClass. It must not be the global default
2. Make the Deployment `queue-worker` in the namespace `jobs` use it

All replicas of `queue-worker` must be running with the new priority.

verification.description: PriorityClass urgent has value 499999 and is not default
queue-worker runs with priority urgent

questions.question:
The node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` is reserved for ML training.

1. Taint it with key `dedicated`, value `ml` and effect `NoSchedule`, and label it `dedicated=ml`
2. In the namespace `ml`, create a Deployment `trainer` with `2` replicas (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that tolerates the taint and only runs on nodes labeled `dedicated=ml` (use a `nodeSelector` or node affinity)

Both Pods must be Running on `k3d-cluster-agent-1`.

verification.description: Node is tainted dedicated=ml:NoSchedule and labeled
trainer tolerates the taint and runs only on the ML node

questions.question:
The namespace `web` exposes the Service `web` (port `80`) through the Ingress `web` with TLS (Secret `web-tls`, host `web.example.local`). Migrate it to the Gateway API. The Gateway API CRDs and a GatewayClass `ckx-gateway` are installed (there is no controller, so only the resources are graded).

1. Create a Gateway `web-gateway` (class `ckx-gateway`) with a listener named `https` on port `443`, protocol `HTTPS`, hostname `web.example.local`, terminating TLS with the Secret `web-tls`
2. Create an HTTPRoute `web-route` attached to `web-gateway` for the hostname `web.example.local` that sends path `/` (`PathPrefix`) to the Service `web` on port `80`
3. Delete the old Ingress `web`

verification.description: Gateway web-gateway terminates TLS for web.example.local on 443
HTTPRoute web-route sends web.example.local/ to web:80
Old Ingress web is deleted

questions.question:
Requests to `http://store.example.local/api` are not reaching the backend. In the namespace `store`, the Ingress `store` is supposed to send `/api` (and everything below it) to the Service `store-api`.

Investigate the Ingress, the Service and its endpoints, and fix the **Ingress** so that it is correct. Do not change the Service or the Deployment.

verification.description: Ingress routes store.example.local/api (Prefix) to store-api:8080
Service and Deployment are unchanged and have endpoints

questions.question:
The Pods `app=frontend` (namespace `frontend`) must reach the Pods `app=backend` (namespace `backend`) on TCP port `80`. A default-deny ingress policy already protects `backend`.

Four candidate policies are in `/tmp/exam/q10/` on `cka-q10`. Apply the **one** that allows exactly this traffic in the **least permissive** way. Do not edit the files and do not apply any of the others.

verification.description: Only policy-3 (allow-frontend-ns) was applied, unmodified

questions.question:
Create a StorageClass named `fast-retain`:

- Provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`
- `reclaimPolicy: Retain`
- `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`
- `allowVolumeExpansion: true`

Make it the **only** default StorageClass of the cluster.

verification.description: fast-retain has the requested settings
fast-retain is the only default StorageClass

questions.question:
The Deployment `catalog` in the namespace `catalog` runs nginx but does not declare any container port.

1. Add the container port `80/TCP` named `http` to its container
2. Create a Service `catalog-np` of type `NodePort` that exposes the Pods on port `80`, targets the **named** port `http`, and uses the node port `30081`

verification.description: Deployment declares containerPort 80 named http
catalog-np is a NodePort 80 -> http on 30081 with endpoints

questions.question:
The Deployment `secure-web` in the namespace `secure-web` serves HTTPS with nginx. Its configuration comes from the ConfigMap `secure-web-conf`, which currently allows `TLSv1.2` and `TLSv1.3`.

1. Change the configuration so that **only TLSv1.3** is accepted
2. Make the running Pods use the new configuration

Verify from inside the cluster, for example from the Pod `tls-client`:
`curl -sk --tls-max 1.2 https://secure-web` must fail and `curl -sk --tlsv1.3 https://secure-web` must work.

verification.description: ConfigMap only allows TLSv1.3
TLS 1.2 is refused and TLS 1.3 works

questions.question:
The Pods of the Deployment `report-api` in the namespace `reports` are stuck in `Pending`.

Find out why, then **patch** the Deployment (do not delete or recreate it) so that its container has:

- requests: CPU `250m`, memory `256Mi`
- limits: CPU `500m`, memory `512Mi`

Both replicas must be Running, and the Deployment must keep its rollout history (it must not be recreated).

verification.description: Requests and limits are set as requested on the original Deployment
Both replicas are Running
